findings.title: Unverified operational years were coerced into publication-year fields
evidence: The formal corpus records H&M year=2022 and Complete Journey year=2014.
The verified registry records year=null for both resources, and the annotated bibliography cites both as n.d.
non_source_metadata.note states that the values are operational-resource years used to satisfy the ARS corpus schema while exact release/edition metadata remains unresolved.
The ARS literature-corpus contract defines year as publication year and requires rejection rather than placeholder coercion when a year cannot be determined.
findings.rationale: Knowingly inserting non-bibliographic operational values into a publication-year field makes the formal corpus internally inconsistent and can contaminate recency filters, counts, and reference export. This is a contract and metadata-integrity defect, not merely missing optional metadata.
remediation: Move H&M and Complete Journey into a separate operational-resource registry until verified edition years exist, or adopt a reviewed resource schema with nullable year plus explicit operational_year and year_basis.
Recompute corpus, recent-source, peer-review, and downstream synthesis summaries.
Regenerate the manifest and pre-audit seal, then submit the new packet for independent re-audit.

findings.title: Jannach and Chen editorial is counted as proven peer-reviewed research
evidence: DOI 10.1145/3800587, authors, year, journal, and volume/issue are verified.
The official ACM content describes the work as an essay/editorial and the authors' institutional record classifies it as Contribution to journal - Editorial.
The packet provides no evidence that this editorial underwent formal external peer review.
findings.rationale: Publication in a peer-reviewed journal does not by itself prove that an editorial article type was formally peer reviewed. The work remains an authoritative standards/position source, but the 49-source peer-reviewed summary is unsupported.
remediation: Set peer_reviewed to false or unknown unless the journal confirms formal external review.
Recompute the peer-reviewed total to at most 48 pending proof.

The affected identities still resolve through DOI and title context, but the stored bibliographic strings are not production-safe.

remediation: Normalize the affected fields from authoritative metadata.

findings.title: Prevalence wording exceeds the targeted and non-exhaustive corpus
evidence: The review is explicitly targeted and non-exhaustive.
C-DATA-EXT-01 and the synthesis matrix say text-rich sources often lack specified signals and order-rich sources often omit others.
findings.rationale: The word often reads as an unbounded prevalence claim about the literature rather than a statement limited to the reviewed candidate set.
remediation: Use the production wording: Among the reviewed candidates, text-rich sources... and preserve the targeted-search qualifier.

findings.title: Evidence convergence count does not qualify dependent source families

artifact_locations.pointer: Evidence convergence map > Vietnamese/external compatibility - 12 sources

evidence: The convergence map states 12 sources without identifying them as canonical corpus records.
RelBench rel-amazon depends on Amazon Reviews, RelBench rel-hm depends on H&M, and adapter/package layers are not independent corroboration.
MNC-8 explicitly prohibits counting RelBench adapters and upstream datasets as independent evidence.
findings.rationale: The unqualified count can overstate evidence convergence despite correct dependence records elsewhere in the packet.
remediation: Report 12 canonical corpus records and state that the number of independent data/source families is lower.
Name the dependent lineages and avoid a numeric family total until a counting rule is frozen.

findings.title: Claim alignment is not source-content or locator verified
evidence: All 21 claim rows depend on lane cards or official summaries.
source_acquired=true is 0/55; source_verified_against_original=true is 0/55; source_verification_method=none is 55/55.
All 30 synthesis citation anchors are anchor:none.
findings.rationale: Identity and summary-level alignment cannot authorize production claims. The packet discloses this limitation, so it is an expected separate gate rather than a concealed Stage 1B defect.
remediation: Acquire and verify the 24-source core set listed in independent_audit_report.md.
Record durable non-null locators and re-run claim-level alignment.
Apply the same rule to any additional source used in production prose.

findings.title: One-shot claim-intent ordering is structurally plausible but not independently auditable

artifact_locations.pointer: root status and first prose block

evidence: Claim IDs, constraint IDs, and planned references pass structural checks.
Declared and filesystem timestamps are consistent with manifest-before-synthesis order.
The frozen packet has no immutable invocation ledger or hash chain proving pre-prose emission and no later mutation.
findings.rationale: A self-declared emitted_at field is not an independent temporal or immutability witness. This is a traceability limitation, not evidence of an actual contract violation.
remediation: Persist a write-once invocation ledger containing manifest hash/time, synthesis start time, and final output hash for future synthesis runs.

findings.title: Complete Journey terms and edition relationship are not snapshotted
evidence: The frozen artifact correctly refuses to treat package CC0 as an upstream dataset grant.
The provider describes about 2,500 households over two years; the package describes 2,469 households over one year.
The packet does not archive contemporaneous provider terms, an exact package revision, or the mapping between the two resource descriptions.
findings.rationale: Availability and package licensing do not establish provider redistribution rights or edition equivalence.
remediation: Archive the provider URL, access time, exact terms bytes, download revision and checksums, and package commit/version.
Obtain institutional/legal review before acquisition sharing, execution, or redistribution.
